vocabulary.meaning_en: the mark ' that shows missing letters (or possession)
vocabulary.example: In "don't", the apostrophe replaces the letter o.

vocabulary.meaning_en: two words joined into one short word, with missing letters

vocabulary.example: The apostrophe shows a missing letter.
In speech, people sometimes drop the "g": doin'.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very informal words used by some groups
serious and correct, for essays and official documents
vocabulary.example: Don't write "goin'" in a formal essay.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way you say a word
vocabulary.example: "Doin'" and "doing" have different pronunciation but the same meaning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: owning something (the apostrophe's other job: James's book)
vocabulary.example: The apostrophe in "James's park" shows possession.
Nice threads! Is that a new shirt?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a quicker way of doing something
vocabulary.example: Contractions are a shortcut in speech.

fine_lines.title: doing vs doin'
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى نفسه، لكن doin' نطق عامّي يُحذف فيه حرف g. في doing ينزل اللسان إلى أسفل الفم، وفي doin' يرتفع إلى سقف الفم. لا تكتب doin' في الكتابة الرسمية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning; "doin'" is a colloquial pronunciation with the g dropped. In "doing" the tongue goes down; in "doin'" it touches the top of the mouth. Don't write "doin'" in formal writing.

fine_lines.title: I'd = I would / I had
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I'd اختصار I would في هذا الدرس (I'd like). قد تعني أيضًا I had. في الكلام نقول I'd، وفي الأسلوب الرسمي I would.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I'd" is short for "I would" here (I'd like). It can also mean "I had". In speech we say I'd; in formal style, I would.

examples.sentence: I would like some coffee, please. (formal)

expressions.meaning_en: A very informal way to say "How are you doing?"

expressions.example: I'd like some coffee and a sandwich, please.

expressions.meaning_en: Where have you been all day?
expressions.example: Where've you been all day? I called you three times.
We're going to the shop. We'll be back later.

grammar.title: The apostrophe shows missing letters
grammar.explanation_ar: الفاصلة العليا (') تخبرنا أن هناك حروفًا محذوفة. ولها وظيفة أخرى هي الملكية (James's book) وهي درس آخر.
grammar.explanation_en: The apostrophe (') tells us some letters are missing. Its other job is possession (James's book), which is another lesson.

grammar.title: Dropping the g in -ing (spoken only)
grammar.explanation_ar: في الكلام غير الرسمي قد يُحذف g من نهاية الفعل المستمر: going → goin', saying → sayin'. المعنى لا يتغير، يتغير النطق فقط. تراه في القصص والأغاني، لكن لا تستعمله في الكتابة الرسمية.
grammar.explanation_en: In informal speech, people may drop the g of -ing: going → goin', saying → sayin'. The meaning stays the same; only the pronunciation changes. You see it in stories, but don't use it in formal writing.
examples: Are you goin' to the party? = Are you going to the party?
What is she sayin'? = What is she saying?

grammar.title: Contractions: two words become one
grammar.explanation_ar: في الاختصار تندمج كلمتان في كلمة واحدة وتُحذف بعض الحروف: are not → aren't، I would → I'd، they have → they've، we will → we'll، do not → don't. الكلمة الجديدة لها نطقها الخاص، فلا تحاول نطق الكلمتين كاملتين. نستعملها لأننا نقول هذه الكلمات كثيرًا جدًا.
grammar.explanation_en: In a contraction, two words join into one and some letters go: are not → aren't, I would → I'd, they have → they've, we will → we'll, do not → don't. The new word has its own sound, so don't try to say both full words. We use them because we say these words very often.
examples: Aren't you hot in that sweater?
I don't know if I'd help him.

grammar.title: Pronunciation tips
grammar.explanation_ar: I'll: قل eye ثم ارفع اللسان إلى سقف الفم: l. she'd: بياء طويلة. aren't: مثل حرف r ثم nt. don't: بحرف o طويل (دونت) وليس dun't.
grammar.explanation_en: I'll: say "eye", then put your tongue up for "l". She'd: long "ee". Aren't: like the letter R + nt. Don't: long "o", not "dun't".
examples: I'll have fries with my burger.
